_meta.description: 2011 mega-flood per-province GISTDA flooded AGRICULTURAL area (hectares), from ERIA Discussion Paper 2013-34 'Impact of the 2011 Floods, and Flood Management in Thailand' Table 2 (MOAC/GISTDA/DDPM). Kept as a cited artifact and for the discrimination analysis — NOT used as a scored event.
_meta.source: ERIA-DP-2013-34.pdf, Table 2 (column GISTDA2, flooded agricultural area, hectares)
why_not_a_scored_event: Metric mismatch: this is flooded *agricultural* area (a subset), not the total per-province flooded area used for the 2022/2021 gold — mixing them would violate METHODOLOGY.md.
Universe incomplete: the table lists selected provinces; upper-Chao-Phraya (Tak, Kamphaeng Phet, Sukhothai, Uttaradit, Phetchabun) are absent, so a full 23-province gold cannot be built.

Non-discriminating: every listed in-basin province flooded far above the 10,000-rai cutoff (see values) — 2011 has ~0 in-basin negatives, so specificity is undefined and a 'predict-everything' baseline (entity) is nearly correct. The causal advantage appears on DISCRIMINATING events (partial floods with real negatives, e.g. 2022/2021), not on a near-universal catastrophe.

Regime change: the King's Dyke that protected Bangkok/Nonthaburi in 2022 was OVERWHELMED in 2011 (both flooded), so the protection flag would have to be event-specific — a real modelling point, documented.

note: Even Bangkok (52,536 ha = 328,350 rai) and Nonthaburi (120,299 ha) — negatives in 2022/2021 — are large positives in 2011. This is the concrete evidence that 2011 is non-discriminating for this benchmark.
